# AI Initiatives Roadmap Table Alignment with Tereza Foltýnová

**Date**: 2026-09-14
**Attendees**: Tereza Foltýnová (ViaPharma CZE — logistics/claims data consolidation), Jindřich Tůma (BigHub — Dr. Max account coordination), Jan Sovka (BigHub — account lead), Marek Pillár (BigHub — PM)
**Type**: external
**Recording**: N/A (transcript only)
**Previous session**: N/A — first meeting under this specific title/attendee combination
**Meeting prep**: [2026-09-14-ai-initiatives-business-quantification-prep.md](../prep/2026-09-14-ai-initiatives-business-quantification-prep.md)

## TL;DR

This was meant to be the live Business Quantification workshop (per prep doc) filling FTE/Kč values for all 11 Žůrke/logistics initiatives — instead it turned into a governance conversation: Tereza raised confusion and mild staff anxiety around a budget-annex table where FTE savings read as headcount cuts, and the team agreed on naming conventions (bilingual CZ/EN columns, Core/Ecom in the title), a simpler business-facing progress format (fraction-of-scope %, not implementation detail), and business-owner sign-off as the process going forward. The actual quantification work was narrowed and deferred: only Reklamace and Fakturace (doprav/od dodavatelů — still ambiguously one or two initiatives) will be walked through this week; the other 9 initiatives wait. After Tereza dropped off, an internal follow-up between Jindřich, Jan Sovka, and Marek surfaced real tension over how much of Marek's time should go into filling this cross-cutting table versus going deep on the two active projects — unresolved, but Marek's concern was heard.

## Key Discussion Points

### The budget-table confusion and staff anxiety

Tereza opened by sharing a table BigHub sent that had become "kind of a chimera" internally — it was originally a budget annex, so the FTE figures next to each initiative got read literally as "once this ships, that FTE gets cut." She stressed this wasn't a complaint about the numbers themselves ("není problém, jako v těch číslech, u toho FTEčka, jakože by si to někdo vycucal z prstů" — *[translated from Czech]* "it's not a problem with the FTE numbers themselves, like someone made them up") — she traced them back to a prior round with "Albena" — but that not everyone had filled in their own figures, and the table's original purpose (budget line-item) didn't match how BigHub now wants to use it (general business-value argument for prioritization).

Jindřich framed the intended purpose plainly: "potřebuje nějaký soustředěný jedno místo, seznam registr těch iniciativ. A business potřebuje mít nějaký průvodní informace k tomu, aby rozhodlo, co má prioritu" *[translated from Czech]* — a single registry of initiatives, with enough business context for Dr. Max to decide what's a priority. Whether that then feeds into actual budgeting is a separate, later step, not this table's job.

### Two parallel tracking documents

Jindřich flagged that Tereza's table looked visually different from the one he'd been shown, despite supposedly sharing a source. Marek confirmed BigHub's copy has no time-saving/FTE column at all for most initiatives. Jan Sovka explained the origin: the FTE/8h-per-day figures came from an early, one-off logistics AI-initiative kickoff meeting with all department heads present — those numbers were never propagated back into Dr. Max's/Tomáš Dudaško's tracked table. BigHub built and has maintained its own separate "source of truth" version for roughly three months of work with Tomáš, independent of whatever Tereza's side later annotated. Jindřich committed to reconciling both documents so the same information is consistent across them (see Action Items).

### Naming and labeling requests

Tereza raised three requests, explicitly framed as "put this in quotes, this caused some panic, not a big deal":
- **Core vs. Ecom scope** should be visible per initiative — doesn't need its own column, can go in the initiative name/title.
- **Bilingual naming** (Czech + English, two columns) — her team has been informally naming things inconsistently ("reklamace" vs. "Receiving Complaints") and it's caused friction; Jindřich agreed this is fair and worth adding, partly because BDC-facing communication sometimes needs English anyway.
- **Reklamace should show as 5 parts, not one line** — today's table reads as if "reklamace" is one monolithic initiative; in reality only the first of five planned sub-parts (direct customer complaints) is in testing. She's worried the client-facing team ends up "s nožem na krku" *[translated from Czech]* (with a knife to the throat) — expected to already be fully live when only 20% is done.

Jindřich's proposed resolution: keep the business-facing table intentionally shallow — "když máme jednu pětinu, tak je to 20%" *[translated from Czech]* ("if we have one-fifth, that's 20%") — and push any deeper explanation of what those five parts are into a popsek/description field or down to the project level, where PM-to-PM detail belongs.

### Business ownership and sign-off

Jindřich pushed for each initiative to eventually get a named business owner who gives a final "palec nahoru" (thumbs up) confirming the numbers are correct — format flexible (email, meeting, whatever Tereza prefers), but the confirmation itself is required before the table is considered reliable.

Asked directly whether Rudolf Žůrek (STK-024) is the business owner for both Reklamace and Fakturace, Tereza was explicit: **"Ne, bude tam Petr Spilka za to. Ruda tam vůbec nebude."** *[translated from Czech]* ("No, Petr Spilka will be the one for that. Ruda won't be involved at all.") She then confirmed: transport/freight → "Ježíšek" (matches Jan Žižka, STK-015, already recorded as owning Fakturace doprav), reklamace → Petr Spilka — who is **already an existing stakeholder, STK-014** (Head of Logistics CORE, previously recorded as owning Reklamace + Fakturace doprav and as "reviewer" on the freight-invoicing scope). Today's statement upgrades his role from reviewer to the actual business-owner sign-off contact for Reklamace specifically. **This directly contradicts the current record for STK-024 (Rudolf Žůrek, listed as "Owner/Customer" for both Reklamace and Invoicing) and narrows the existing three-way Reklamace attribution (Žůrek / Petr Spilka, STK-014 / Marie Hulešová, STK-020) toward Spilka** — flagged for PM resolution in the routing review below.

Tereza declined to convene all three business owners together on short notice ("To já jako je nedám, takhle dohromady narychlo") but agreed to bring the two active-initiative owners (reklamace, fakturace) into a working session this week.

### Marek's proposed working method going forward

Marek proposed sending Tereza a short framework of interview-style questions ahead of time (what's happening in the department, why the initiative exists, what would you want different) — she fills what she can herself and escalates the rest to the actual business owners, then they walk through the answers together, initiative by initiative, filling one table at a time. Tereza welcomed this ("To je skvělý" / "That's great") but flagged upfront that she won't have adequate answers to every question herself and will need to loop in owners regardless.

### Internal follow-up: scope and depth of Marek's onboarding work (after Tereza left)

Once Tereza dropped off the call, Jindřich, Jan Sovka, and Marek continued discussing how Marek should actually spend this week. Marek raised a direct concern: if he spends the week filling a "top-management Excel" across 8-9 streams without going deep on any single project, he risks repeating a pattern he says has already happened once — investing real time into a deliverable that turns out disconnected from what actually matters to him in the PM role ("já jsem to komunikoval s Jindro věckrát... nebylo to raz" — *[translated from Czech]* "I've told Jindra this before, more than once, this isn't the first time"). He was explicit that this isn't his usual way of working, though he'll follow the direction he's given.

Jindřich's position: the table work is a genuine, ongoing part of Marek's role, not a one-off distraction, and reading the underlying spec plus running the two owner meetings this week doubles as real onboarding — Marek doesn't need deep historical background to do it, since the owners themselves will supply that context conversationally. Jan Sovka broadly agreed with Jindřich on substance but was candid that the client narrative (Tomáš Dudaško's framing: reklamace and fakturace work "should already be done," now it's about showing forward motion) is real pressure regardless of whether Marek finds the exercise valuable personally — "Fast and Furious," in his words. No firm resolution was reached; the practical landing point was: this week narrows to scheduling and holding the two owner meetings (reklamace, fakturace), treated as onboarding, with the other ~36 rows/9 initiatives explicitly deferred to a later "Part B" once business direction is clearer.

## Decisions Made

- Jindřich Tůma and Marek Pillár are the joint owners of the AI-initiatives roadmap/table effort going forward — Marek actively works on it, Jindřich reviews.
- The business-facing roadmap table stays intentionally shallow: simple fraction-of-scope completion (e.g., "1 of 5 parts done = 20%"), with deeper explanation pushed to a description field or the project level — not spelled out in the top-level table.
- Reklamace will be explicitly represented as 5 sub-parts in the table, with current progress shown as 1 of 5, to prevent the client team from assuming full-scope delivery.
- Initiative names will carry both a Czech and an English label (two columns).
- Core vs. Ecom scope will be indicated in the initiative name/title rather than as a separate column.
- This week's active quantification scope narrows to 2 initiatives — Reklamace and Fakturace (doprav/od dodavatelů) — validating FTE figures and confirming business-owner sign-off; the other 9 Žůrek/logistics initiatives are explicitly deferred, not dropped.
- Deep quantification of the remaining ~36 non-logistics rows, and any new 2027 initiative planning, is deferred to a later phase pending clearer business direction from Dr. Max.

## Sentiment & Tone

Collaborative and self-aware throughout the client-facing portion — Tereza repeatedly softened her own critiques ("berte to v uvozovkách," "jenom prosím") and was careful to say the FTE numbers weren't fabricated, just misapplied to the wrong document. The underlying anxiety is real, though: budget season, headcount sensitivity ("jakmile někomu šáhneš do těch FTE, tak už jsou všichni naježený" — once you touch anyone's FTEs, everyone bristles), and fragmented cross-team naming have created friction that isn't really about BigHub's work quality. She closed warmly, thanking the team and expressing hope the table finally gets unified ("ať to jede už pro boha"). Jindřich stayed consistently upbeat and solution-oriented ("já jsem optimista"), reassuring her that this is a shared, ongoing communication problem rather than a one-sided failure.

The internal (BigHub-only) segment after Tereza left had a different, more unresolved texture: Marek raised a genuine, specific concern about how his time is being directed, referencing a prior similar situation. Jindřich held his position firmly but respectfully; Jan Sovka acted as a bridge, validating Marek's discomfort as reasonable while also naming the external pressure (Dudaško's framing) that makes the shallow, fast approach necessary for now. Nothing was resolved adversarially, but this is the first visible instance of friction between Marek's own working instincts and the direction being set for him — worth watching in future 1:1s.
